purpose: Test whether deliberately induced changes that increase measured objective drift reproduce the drift-difficulty relationship found in the nominal sequences. Not a second benchmark suite.

system_choice_reason.hvac: nominal sequence is completely benign (0 of 1500 transitions non-benign), so any induced drift is unambiguous
system_choice_reason.uav: largest natural tail drift and the only system with clear optimizer separation

process_disturbance.hvac: additive state disturbance, sigma = 0.05 K per step on the three room temperature states (about 2.5% of the 2 K setpoint offset)
process_disturbance.uav: additive state disturbance, sigma = 0.02 m per step on the three position states (0.2% of the 10 m reference travel)

measurement_noise.hvac: sigma = 0.05 K on the state passed to the controller only; the true plant state is unperturbed
measurement_noise.uav: sigma = 0.02 m on the position states passed to the controller only

reference_event.hvac: room setpoints step by +1.0 K at 50% of the horizon
reference_event.uav: position reference steps by +1.0 m in x at 50% of the horizon

magnitude_rationale: Each magnitude is a small fraction of the quantity the controller is regulating, chosen to be physically plausible and NOT tuned to induce optimizer failure. They were fixed before any optimizer result was observed.
trajectory_length_reason: Bounded to 400 steps per system so the study stays small; the nominal condition is rerun at the same length so all comparisons are like-for-like.
